crop.notes: Headline ('Ed Smith's Victory. The Denver Man Put Goddard to Rest in the Eighteenth Round') and opening paragraph are missing at the top; the clipping ends at Round 9 and the rest of the fight continues in the next column

title.suggested: Tom Allen Seconds Ed Smith Against Joe Goddard in New Orleans

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen, in a shiny silk hat and diamond stud, was one of Ed Smith's seconds when the Denver heavyweight beat Joe Goddard in 18 rounds at New Orleans.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, March 4, 1893; dispatch datelined New Orleans, March 3; Olympic Club carnival

facts.fact: Allen was one of Ed Smith's seconds (with Bat Masterson, Jack Fogarty and Pat Smith) when Smith fought Joe Goddard; Smith won in the eighteenth round
Allen traveled to New Orleans for the Olympic Club carnival to attend the Smith-Goddard fight

notes: Article first says 'Big Tom Allen ... occupied a private box' and 'took more than ordinary interest,' then lists him among Smith's seconds entering the ring; both are in the clipping. The 18th-round result is from the headline on the page, outside the clipping.
